findings.summary: The 80px rise-and-scale entrance on the h1 and p runs for 1.4s with no prefers-reduced-motion fallback.
findings.fix: Add a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) rule that removes the animation, or swaps it for a short opacity-only fade.

findings.summary: The background video autoplays and loops forever, with no reduced-motion check and no pause control.
findings.fix: Skip autoplay or pause the video when prefers-reduced-motion matches, and add a visible pause/play control.

findings.summary: The parallax scroll listener is not passive and writes a transform on every scroll event without requestAnimationFrame throttling.
findings.fix: Register the listener with { passive: true } and batch the transform write in a single requestAnimationFrame per frame, or use a CSS scroll-driven animation.

findings.summary: The scroll-linked parallax layer moves even when the user prefers reduced motion.
findings.fix: Check matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') and skip the parallax transform when it matches.

findings.summary: will-change is set permanently on 24 cards for transform, opacity, top and width, which wastes compositor memory and includes properties that cannot be composited.
findings.fix: Remove the blanket will-change, or limit it to transform and apply it only during interaction.

findings.summary: The hover lift animates top (and the transition also covers width), which triggers layout on every frame.
findings.fix: Animate transform: translateY(-8px) instead of top, and drop width from the transition.

findings.summary: The 'Learn more' links stay at opacity 0 unless the card is hovered, so keyboard users tab onto invisible links.
findings.fix: Also reveal .more on .card:focus-within and on .more:focus-visible.

findings.summary: The links are revealed only on hover, so touch users never see them, or see them stick after a tap.
findings.fix: Show .more by default and gate the hover-reveal behind @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).

findings.summary: The scroll handler calls getBoundingClientRect and then writes style.width on each card in the same loop, forcing layout thrash for 24 cards on every scroll event.
findings.fix: Use an IntersectionObserver to toggle a class, or read all rects first and write in a requestAnimationFrame, and avoid changing width.

findings.summary: The scroll progress bar animates width from an unthrottled, non-passive scroll listener, which triggers layout.
findings.fix: Drive the bar with transform: scaleX() from a passive, rAF-throttled listener, or use a CSS scroll-timeline.

findings.summary: The dialog scale-and-fade transition has no reduced-motion fallback.
findings.fix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove the scale transform and keep only a brief opacity change, or no transition.

findings.summary: button:focus { outline: none } removes the focus indicator from every button and gives no replacement.
findings.fix: Delete the rule, or replace it with a visible :focus-visible outline.

findings.summary: Opening the modal does not move focus into the dialog, trap focus, or support Escape, and the dialog has no dialog role.
findings.fix: Use a native <dialog> with showModal(), or add role=dialog/aria-modal, move focus to the first field, trap Tab and close on Escape.

findings.summary: Closing the modal does not return focus to the 'Sign up' trigger.
findings.fix: Store the opener element when opening and call focus() on it after closing.

findings.summary: The open and close timeouts are never cleared, so reopening within 350ms of closing lets the pending timeout remove 'open' and hide the freshly opened modal.
findings.fix: Keep the timeout IDs and clear them in openModal and closeModal, or use transitionend and check the current state before removing classes.

findings.summary: The counter ticks on every frame no matter what prefers-reduced-motion says.
findings.fix: When reduced motion is preferred, render the final value without the rAF ticking.

findings.summary: The requestAnimationFrame loop never stops and is never cancelled on unmount, so each remount stacks another endless loop, which keeps running against detached nodes.
findings.fix: Store the rAF id, stop at a target value, and call cancelAnimationFrame from a teardown that runs before panel.innerHTML is replaced.

findings.summary: A new IntersectionObserver is created on every mount and never disconnected or unobserved.
findings.fix: Unobserve each element after it reveals, and call io.disconnect() in the stats teardown.

findings.summary: Each mountStats call adds another resize listener that is never removed and keeps references to detached counters.
findings.fix: Keep a named handler and remove it on unmount (or use an AbortController signal), or move the sizing to a CSS media query.

findings.summary: touch-action: none on html and body turns off native touch scrolling and pinch-zoom for the whole page.
findings.fix: Remove touch-action from html and body, and use touch-action: pan-y on the carousel track only if needed.

findings.summary: The slide transition has no reduced-motion fallback.
findings.fix: Set transition: none on .track under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: The carousel controls appear only on hover, so touch users cannot see the dots.
findings.fix: Show controls by default, or reveal them on :focus-within as well, and limit hover-hiding to @media (hover: hover).

findings.summary: The navigation dots are divs with click handlers only, so keyboard users cannot focus or activate them.
findings.fix: Use <button> elements with aria-labels (and aria-current) for the dots, and make them visible on :focus-within.

findings.summary: Slides auto-advance every 3s with no pause control, no pause on hover/focus/hidden tab, and no reduced-motion check.
findings.fix: Turn autoplay off under prefers-reduced-motion, add a pause button, and pause on hover, focus-within and visibilitychange.

findings.summary: The autoplay interval is not reset after a manual dot click or swipe, so the carousel can jump again right after the user acts.
findings.fix: Store the interval ID and clear and restart it (or pause it) whenever go() is triggered by user input.
